## Purpose 
<!--- One sentence to describe the purpose of this PR, refer to any linked issues:
#14 -- this will link to issue 14
Closes #2 -- this will automatically close issue 2 on PR merge
-->
Evaluating the AMIP simulations with #2217 against CERES EBAF Ed4.2.1 showed two remaining physical issues in the prescribed sea-ice model:

1. **Antarctic summer sea-ice albedo is too dark (`0.49–0.57` vs. CERES `0.69–0.73` in Dec–Feb):** Unlike the Arctic, Antarctic sea ice retains snow cover through summer and rarely forms extensive surface melt ponds, keeping broadband albedo higher. Using the Arctic melt-pond value (`α_melt = 0.55`) globally overly darkens Southern Ocean pack ice in austral summer. Note: ERA5 shows a smaller value, but I think CERES is more accurate.
2. **Newly forming seasonal sea ice starts at a stale temperature:** Ice-free grid cells previously kept a fallback (`T_sfc = 261.2 K`, `-12 °C`) or their last pre-melt-out temperature while ice-free, rather than starting at the seawater freezing point (`T_base = 271.2 K`) when seasonal sea ice advances in autumn.

Changes in this PR:

- **Hemispheric summer melt albedo:** Split `α_melt` in `IceSlabParameters` into `α_melt_nh = 0.55` (Arctic melt ponds) and `α_melt_sh = 0.72` (Antarctic wet snow).
- **Freezing-point start for newly forming sea ice:** Reset ice-free grid cells to `T_bulk = T_base` (`T_sfc = 271.2 K`) at initialization and on daily SIC updates so newly formed sea ice always begins at seawater freezing.
- **SIC sanitization on update:** Apply NaN handling, optional binary thresholding, and land clamping immediately when SIC is read daily rather than on every RK4 stage.
